entities.summary:
Sigebert II (601–613), also called Sigisbert II, was the illegitimate son of Theuderic II, from whom he inherited the kingdoms of Burgundy and Austrasia in 613. He was put on the throne by his great-grandmother, Brunhilda, who dominated his short reign.

Sigebert II's ascension to power marked the beginning of the end of the Merovingian dynasty, which had ruled the Frankish Kingdom since the 5th century. His reign was marked by power struggles with the Church and the nobility, as well as military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms.

Despite his short and tumultuous reign, Sigebert II's legacy continued to shape the course of European history. His kingdoms of Burgundy and Austrasia became important centers of trade and culture, and his legacy influenced the development of the Holy Roman Empire.

The death of Sigebert II in 613 marked the end of the Merovingian dynasty, but his impact on European history continued to be felt for centuries to come.
